stories.title: Manifest Global acquires Mindler career guidance business
stories.summary: Manifest Global has acquired the career guidance business of India-based Mindler. The companies partnered for a year before the deal, which aims to test the view that career exploration should precede university choice. Mindler founder Prateek Bhargava will continue to run the business under the new ownership.

stories.title: Graduate job market concerns rise alongside AI
stories.summary: Dr Armin D Ashenberg of Western Sydney University is examining how educational institutions should respond to AI impacting the graduate experience. A July federal government report identified jobs involving cognitive tasks as those most at risk, as AI systems continue to match or exceed human performance in intellectual tasks.

stories.title: Study abroad applications face increasing competition
stories.summary: More than 1.2 million Indian students studied abroad in 2025, a figure expected to rise. However, shifting immigration policies and evolving regulations have made the application process more competitive. Experts suggest that a well-prepared application communicating academic interests and career goals is now essential for prospective international students.

stories.title: Rollins College offers MBA path for inexperienced graduates
stories.summary: Many MBA programs require significant work experience, leaving recent graduates in limbo. The Crummer Graduate School of Business at Rollins College has introduced a solution for those lacking professional history. It accepts inexperienced students into programs that require them to build the specific experience employers currently demand.

stories.title: Obstacles persist in the community college transfer pipeline
stories.summary: National data suggests that while 80 percent of community college students plan to transfer to a four-year institution, only 32 percent do so. Of those, fewer than half earn a bachelor’s degree. Institutions often create obstacles in the transfer pipeline without realizing they are doing so.

stories.title: Schools urged to focus on human skills for AI-proof workforce
stories.summary: As AI becomes common in the workplace, the conversation regarding job security is shifting. A recent report suggests that the best way for K-12 students to prepare is by leaning into human strengths like empathy and judgment, which are increasingly requested in roles exposed to artificial intelligence.

stories.title: Stopped-out student population reaches 37.8 million
stories.summary: The number of people who have left higher education without completing a degree has reached 37.8 million. According to the National Student Clearinghouse Research Center, approximately 1.9 million of these individuals departed from their studies recently.

stories.title: North Country students express AI career concerns
stories.summary: Around 130 employers gathered at Watertown International Airport to conduct mock interviews with high school seniors. While students described the experience as positive, many noted that their primary concern regarding entering the workforce is the increasing use of artificial intelligence in professional roles.

stories.title: Insider Information: College Students Weigh In on AI's Impact on Careers and Coursework - U.S. News & World Report
Three students receive 2026 Giller Mantella Scholarship
stories.summary: Audrey Gignac, Sofia Cina, and Sarah-Marie Scale have been named recipients of the 2026 Giller Mantella Scholarship. The program supports Black, Indigenous, and racialized students pursuing post-secondary studies in English literature and creative writing. The scholarship includes a spotlight event with acclaimed Canadian writers.

stories.title: Northwestel announces 2026 scholarship recipients
stories.summary: Northwestel has awarded six northern students a $4,000 scholarship to support their post-secondary education. The program covers fields ranging from engineering to accounting. Recipients are also offered a 2027 placement with the company, as the firm aims to encourage young people to study, grow, and return home.

stories.title: Student achieves national recognition in mathematics
stories.summary: Nguyen Thi Ha Trang, a student at the Vietnam Academy of Agriculture, has been recognized as a national 5 Good Student. A former high-scoring entrance exam candidate, she has earned five medals in the National Mathematical Olympiad while pursuing a degree in technology education.

Armenian students secure medals at astronomy olympiad
stories.summary: All six members of Armenia’s team won medals at the International Open Astronomy Olympiad in Russia. The group secured two gold and four silver medals among 69 competitors from 14 countries. The event was held in the Sirius Federal Territory from November 6 to 14.

stories.title: OHL announces 2026 leadership scholarship winners
stories.summary: Four students have been named recipients of the 2026 David Branch Leadership Scholarship. Each will receive $5,000 toward their post-secondary education. The program, now in its second year, honors the legacy of the late OHL commissioner and is supported by Special Olympics Ontario.

stories.title: Bangladesh second in Geography Olympiad, wins five medals - Banglanews24
Jharkhand students present vocational skill models
stories.summary: Over 200 government school students in Jharkhand showcased vocational models at a state-level exhibition. Officials stated that vocational education may eventually begin as early as the sixth grade. The initiative is part of a broader move toward competency-based learning under the National Education Policy 2020.

stories.title: European Space Agency opens 2027 student program
stories.summary: The European Space Agency has opened applications for its 2027 student program. The initiative offers university students the opportunity to gain professional experience across science, engineering, and business sectors. Participants work alongside professionals in an international environment to develop practical skills for the space industry.

stories.title: CERN opens 2027 summer student programme
stories.summary: CERN is inviting undergraduate and Master’s students to Geneva for its 2027 summer programme. Participants will work on technical and scientific projects alongside international experts while earning 94 Swiss francs per day. The organisation describes the experience as an opportunity to gain practical research skills at a leading institution.

stories.title: IIIT-Hyderabad students build sign language plugin
stories.summary: Two students at IIIT-Hyderabad have developed a browser plugin that translates text into Indian Sign Language in real time. The tool functions without external hardware or server-side AI models. The creators aim to bridge the gap for users with hearing impairments who find standard online content difficult to navigate.

stories.title: How to Write a Winning Cover Letter: 10 Practical Tips to Stand Out and Get Hired
stories.summary: In today’s competitive job market, having an impressive CV is important, but it is not always enough to secure your next opportunity. While your CV highlights your qualifications, professional experience, and achievements, your cover letter gives you the opportunity to explain why those experiences matter and how they make you

stories.summary: In today’s competitive job market, having the right qualifications, skills, and experience is not always enough to secure your dream job. How you present these qualifications to potential employers can make a significant difference in whether you receive an invitation for an interview or another rejection email. Your Curriculum Vitae

stories.summary: CBSE Class 12 Science students preparing for the 2027 board examinations can access the study material to strengthen their preparation in English, Physics, Chemistry, Mathematics and Biology. From the latest syllabus and previous year question papers to sample papers, chapter-wise MCQs and exam pattern, the right study resources can help

stories.summary: The Central Board of Secondary Education (CBSE) has released the Class 10 Sample Question Papers (SQPs) and marking schemes for the academic session 2026-27 to help students prepare for the upcoming board examinations. Students appearing for the CBSE Class 10 Board Exam 2027 can download subject-wise sample papers to understand

stories.summary: The Central Board of Secondary Education (CBSE) has released the Class 12 Sample Question Papers (SQPs) and marking schemes for the academic session 2026-27 to help students prepare for the upcoming board examinations. Students appearing for the CBSE Class 12 Board Exam 2027 can download subject-wise sample papers to understand

stories.title: Schools shift focus toward computational thinking
stories.summary: As schools navigate the integration of AI, India is prioritising foundational skills like logical reasoning and problem-solving. Educators argue that teaching students to prompt a chatbot is insufficient, as interfaces may soon become obsolete. The goal is for students to understand how technology processes information and questions its output.

stories.title: Utah State University hosts academic olympiad
stories.summary: Utah State University welcomed 250 high school students to its campus on November 10 for the 2026-2027 Academic Olympiad. Participants from nearly 30 public schools competed in math, social studies, science, and language arts. The event aims to strengthen partnerships between regional school districts and the university.

stories.title: Two KGBV students reach aviation olympiad finals
stories.summary: Two students from Kasturba Gandhi Balika Vidyalaya in Telangana have qualified for the national finals of the Aviation Olympiad. They were selected from a pool of over 2.09 lakh participants across 12,400 schools. The final round will include 145 students from across the country.

stories.title: Alphores institutions announce math olympiad
stories.summary: Alphores Educational Institutions will hold its state-level math olympiad on December 6 and 15 across Telangana. The organisation plans to distribute 4,44,444 rupees in cash prizes on December 22 to mark National Mathematics Day. Posters for the event were released at the institution's central office in Karimnagar.

stories.title: Turkmenistan institute announces finance olympiad winners
stories.summary: The Turkmen State Institute of Economics and Management has announced the winners of its third international internet olympiad in finance. Approximately 200 students from 11 countries participated, completing 10 tasks in 120 minutes. The competition was conducted in Turkmen, English, and Russian languages.

stories.title: International finance olympiad awards 121 prizes
stories.summary: The Turkmen State Institute of Economics and Management awarded 121 prizes following its third international internet olympiad in finance. Participants from 52 institutions competed, with 24 first-place, 41 second-place, and 56 third-place diplomas issued. Each student had two hours to answer 10 questions on the subject.

stories.title: University of Idaho launches rural scholarship program
stories.summary: The University of Idaho has established the Harry L. Bettis Scholarship Program to support students from rural communities. Partnering with the Harry L. Bettis Foundation, the university has already awarded funding to 135 students. Applicants must graduate from a rural high school and enroll as full-time students.

stories.title: Rest and Resilience Fellowship 2027 opens
stories.summary: Applications are open for the 2027 Rest and Resilience Fellowship, which offers two journalists a six-month stay in Berlin. The program is designed for media professionals working in countries with restricted press freedoms. Participants may choose to withdraw from public life or attend professional workshops during their stay.

stories.title: Apps Open for Next Gen Scholarship
stories.summary: (Indianapolis, IN) to Applications are now being accepted for the Next Generation Hoosier Educator Scholarship. The Next Gen scholarship is designed to lower the cost of college for aspiring teachers while strengthening the state’s educator workforce. Officials say, by reducing financial barriers, the scholarship helps more Hoosiers enter high‑demand education

stories.title: INSPIRE-SHE scholarship applications open until December 7
stories.summary: The Department of Science and Technology is accepting applications for 12,000 INSPIRE-SHE scholarships. The program supports meritorious students pursuing undergraduate and postgraduate science degrees. Eligibility is based on performance in national-level exams or Class 12 board results. The deadline to apply is December 7, 2026.

stories.title: American Open University launches N760 million scholarship
stories.summary: American Open University and the American College of Technology are launching the O’GIFTS scholarship scheme. The program provides N760 million in tuition support for 500 Ogbomoso students over five years. The initiative, named for the Soun of Ogbomosoland, will be launched virtually on November 24, 2026.

stories.title: MTSU concludes True Blue Tour with $500,000 in scholarships
stories.summary: Middle Tennessee State University finished its 2026 recruitment tour after awarding over $500,000 in scholarships. President Sidney A. McPhee led the final trip, which showcased 300 undergraduate and graduate degree programs. The tour included 10 stops across Tennessee and Alabama to attract prospective students.

stories.title: University of California regents debate SAT return
stories.summary: The University of California Board of Regents met to discuss reinstating SAT and ACT exams. Researchers presented conflicting views on whether the tests predict academic success or primarily benefit wealthier students. Students protested the potential return of the exams. The board took no action during the meeting.

stories.title: Kentucky returns to ACT for state college admissions
stories.summary: Kentucky will switch back to the ACT for its state-funded college admissions exam in 2027. The Department of Education awarded a four-year contract to ACT at $28.50 per student. The state previously paid $38 per student for the ACT before a one-year trial with the SAT.

stories.title: After just one year using SAT, Kentucky goes back to ACT for college admission exam - Lexington Herald Leader
Kentucky switches back to ACT for state exams
stories.summary: Kentucky will return to the ACT for its state-funded college admissions exam in 2027. The state cited a 2026 law requiring competitive procurement, noting the ACT is now cheaper than the SAT. The new contract costs $28.50 per student, a reduction from the previous $30 SAT rate.

stories.title: Kentucky high school juniors to take ACT in 2027
stories.summary: Kentucky will resume using the ACT as its state-funded college admissions exam for public school juniors. The state reversed its previous switch to the SAT, citing a new four-year contract at $28.50 per student. The exam remains free for all public school juniors regardless of college plans.

stories.title: Rajasthan CET 12th level admit cards available November 26
stories.summary: The Rajasthan Staff Selection Board will release provisional e-admit cards for the Common Eligibility Test on November 26. The examination is scheduled for December 1, 2, and 3 across two daily shifts. Registered candidates can access their hall tickets through the official recruitment portal.

stories.title: Telangana board releases 2027 intermediate exam schedule
stories.summary: The Telangana Board of Intermediate Education has released the tentative timetable for 2027 public examinations. First-year exams are scheduled from February 24 to March 19, while second-year exams run from February 25 to March 20. The full schedule is available on the board website.

stories.title: Rajasthan CET 12th level exam details released
stories.summary: The Rajasthan Staff Selection Board will provide examination district details on November 21, followed by e-admit cards on November 26. The Common Eligibility Test for senior secondary students will take place from December 1 to 3. Candidates can access their information through the official SSO portal.

stories.title: UGC NET December 2026 exam schedule announced
stories.summary: The University Grants Commission has released the schedule for the December 2026 National Eligibility Test. Exams will take place from December 14 to 18 and on December 21. The tests will be conducted in two daily shifts. The commission also recently identified 32 fake universities.

stories.title: Telangana board issues 2027 intermediate exam timetable
stories.summary: The Telangana Board of Intermediate Education has published the tentative timetable for February and March 2027 examinations. Theory tests for first and second-year students begin on February 24 and 25, respectively. The schedule includes practical assessments and compulsory examinations for all participating students.

stories.title: Assam board sets 2027 exam dates
stories.summary: The Assam State School Education Board has scheduled Class 10 examinations to begin on February 25, with Class 12 exams following on March 12, 2027. Students can access the full timetable and subject-specific instructions through the board's official websites.

stories.title: Assam finalizes Class 10 exam schedule
stories.summary: The Assam State School Education Board will begin Class 10 final examinations on February 25. The schedule follows an extension of classroom teaching hours intended to compensate for academic disruptions caused by floods and Census-related activities earlier this year.

stories.title: International student enrollment drops at Wichita State
stories.summary: International student enrollment is declining at Wichita State University, mirroring a national trend of a 9 percent decrease. The university has discontinued its dedicated Saturday enrollment event due to low numbers, as advisors point to rising costs and visa processing delays as primary factors.

stories.title: Japanese firms seek international graduates
stories.summary: Japanese companies are increasingly recruiting international students to address local labor shortages. Despite the demand, many candidates remain unable to secure positions due to stringent employer requirements, specifically regarding Japanese language proficiency.

stories.title: Judge rejects four-year visa limit
stories.summary: A federal judge has struck down a Department of Homeland Security rule that would have capped student visa stays at four years. The ruling preserves the longstanding duration of status policy, allowing international students to remain in the country for the length of their academic programs.

stories.title: Courts block visa and training restrictions
stories.summary: Federal judges have issued injunctions blocking two August 2026 directives that narrowed eligibility for Curricular Practical Training and capped student visa stays at four years. The court found the visa cap rule arbitrary and capricious, noting its negative impact on academic mobility.

stories.title: Federal court stays student visa rules
stories.summary: A federal judge has set aside a rule limiting F-1 students to four-year admission periods, while another judge stayed guidance restricting Curricular Practical Training. These rulings prevent the enforcement of the new policies nationwide while the underlying litigation remains pending.

stories.title: Federal Judge Strikes Down Rule Limiting International Students' Stays - The EDU Ledger
Bar Council warns law students on college status
stories.summary: The Bar Council of India has advised prospective law students to verify the affiliation and approval status of institutions before enrolling. The advisory follows a Supreme Court direction aimed at preventing colleges from making misleading claims regarding their legal authority to impart professional education.

stories.title: Ireland grants visas to 48 students from Gaza
stories.summary: The Irish justice minister has granted visas to 48 students from Gaza following a High Court order to review previous application refusals. The court had identified significant errors in the initial handling of the cases. Only 20 students are currently cleared for departure.

stories.title: Irish university funding linked to visa regime
stories.summary: The president of the Technological University of the Shannon told an Oireachtas committee that linking student visas to immigration is a fallacy. Irish universities report that a tighter visa regime introduced this year is negatively impacting their ability to secure necessary funding.

stories.title: Gaza students receive Irish study visas
stories.summary: Following a High Court order to reconsider 60 refusal decisions, the Irish Minister for Justice has granted visas to 48 students from Gaza. While all students hold fully funded scholarships, only 20 are currently scheduled for evacuation from the territory.

stories.title: Student visa issuances decline for India and China
stories.summary: F-1 student visa issuances for nationals of India fell 74 percent in the first five months of fiscal year 2026 compared to the previous eight-year average. Issuances for Chinese nationals declined 45 percent over the same period.

stories.title: Court maintains duration of status for students
stories.summary: A federal court has invalidated a plan to limit the duration of international student stays in the U.S. The decision upholds the duration of status practice, which allows students to remain in the country indefinitely while enrolled in an academic degree program.

stories.title: Google ultimatum complicates AI school debate
stories.summary: The debate over AI in K-12 schools has intensified after Google announced that districts banning its AI technology will lose access to its search engine. The move presents a challenge for districts like Chicago that have already phased out AI tools in the classroom.

stories.title: Grants awarded for multilingual AI tools
stories.summary: Three developers will receive 350,000 dollars each to build AI tools for multilingual learners, with pilot programs planned in Colorado, Massachusetts, and Wisconsin. Two-thirds of public school teachers report having at least one multilingual learner in their classroom.

stories.title: How students use AI matters more than whether they use it - District Administration
Punjab to train 25,898 teachers in AI
stories.summary: The Punjab government is launching an AI training program for 25,898 public school teachers beginning November 23. The initiative, organized by the School Education Department and PECTAA, aims to integrate modern technology into primary and elementary classrooms across the province.

stories.title: Catholic school weighs AI against academic honesty and human dignity - The Edwardsville Intelligencer
CISCE launches nationwide digital assessment initiative
stories.summary: The Council for the Indian School Certificate Examinations has launched SHINE 2026, a digital diagnostic programme to identify student learning gaps. Within 48 hours of its November 15 launch, 450 schools participated and the platform recorded three million student responses. The initiative aims to strengthen classroom teaching through targeted interventions.

stories.title: UWindsor researcher examines the changing role of language teachers
stories.summary: As artificial intelligence becomes common in classrooms, University of Windsor PhD student Luyao Tan is exploring how the technology shifts the role of language teachers. Tan, a researcher in the Reciprocal Learning Program, suggests teachers have an opportunity to rethink their contributions regarding cultural understanding and human connection.

stories.title: Kelowna educator says AI shifts classroom focus to process
stories.summary: Derek Cutler, director of innovation at Aberdeen Hall Preparatory School, says artificial intelligence is changing education by making answers instantly available. Consequently, educators are shifting their focus from final answers to the learning process. Cutler notes that AI algorithms are now embedded in everything students do.

stories.title: New York City releases AI guidance for schools
stories.summary: New York City’s Department of Education has implemented a Red-Yellow-Green model to regulate generative AI in schools. Chatbots are forbidden from grading or writing IEPs, while lesson planning is permitted. The policy arrives despite the lack of definitive science regarding the use of generative AI for learning.

stories.title: TCAPS educators focus on AI safety and limitations
stories.summary: Traverse City Area Public Schools is working to teach students how to use artificial intelligence responsibly. The district is coordinating with its curriculum department to select tools that support learning while protecting personal information. The approach currently prioritizes older students, with limited access provided for younger grades.

stories.title: Great Minds in STEM launches AI readiness sessions
stories.summary: Great Minds in STEM has launched a virtual series powered by Walmart to help individuals navigate an AI-driven job market. The first session offered practical guidance on adopting new technologies and strengthening professional skills. The initiative targets those entering the workforce or seeking to remain competitive in changing industries.

stories.title: Former IBO medalist returns to teach at Lam Son Gifted School
stories.summary: Nguyen Dac Hieu, a 2016 IBO bronze medalist, has returned to his alma mater, Lam Son High School for the Gifted, as a biology teacher. His appointment is part of a recruitment drive by the Thanh Hoa Department of Education and Training to staff public educational institutions.

stories.title: Albania trains 20,000 teachers under national programme
stories.summary: Education Minister Mirela Kumbaro announced that over 20,300 teachers have completed the 2026 National Professional Development Programme. The initiative aims to improve teaching practices and integrate artificial intelligence into schools. The 2027 budget will continue funding training in modern teaching methods for the pre-university education sector.

stories.title: Teaching Professionals Council launches in Thimphu
stories.summary: The Ministry of Education and Skills Development in Thimphu has launched the Teaching Professionals Council. The new body is intended to champion the growth, recognition, and professional standing of teachers across the country. The council aims to provide a dedicated platform to strengthen national teaching standards.

stories.title: Rural women train as drone pilots under national scheme
stories.summary: Mantravati Shakya, a rural drone pilot, has trained 50 other women to operate agricultural drones. Her work supports the national Namo Drone Didi scheme, which aims to place drones in the hands of 15,000 women’s self-help groups. The programme encourages participants to share their technical skills within their villages.

stories.title: Digital transformation at École secondaire Vanier
stories.summary: École secondaire Vanier in Québec City has integrated digital technology into its professional development for teachers. The school, which serves 350 students in a disadvantaged area, began the CybernéTIC project in 2014 to shift from targeted digital experiments to a broader transformation of its teaching practices.

stories.title: Report suggests schools should be judged beyond grades
stories.summary: A report by Alan Milburn on the nation's 16 to 24-year-olds not in education, employment or training suggests schools should be judged on more than exam results. The findings argue that schools must be at the heart of the solution to help young people reach their potential.

stories.title: Bodhan AI partners to train one million teachers
stories.summary: Bodhan AI, an IIT Madras-incubated centre, has partnered with three education groups to train one million teachers in AI literacy. The 12 to 18-month initiative focuses on using AI for lesson planning, content creation, and administrative tasks. The programme will be implemented with support from the Learning Links Foundation.

stories.title: Uzbekistan discusses teacher training with international partners
stories.summary: Officials in Uzbekistan met with representatives from the Cambridge Partnership for Education and UNICEF to discuss teacher professional development. The talks focused on introducing modern teaching methods and expanding training opportunities. The meeting was held at the Republican Scientific and Methodological Centre for Education Development in Tashkent.

stories.title: Vietnam emphasizes development of military teachers
stories.summary: The Vietnamese government has identified the development of a contingent of military teachers as a key priority for the Vietnam People’s Army. The policy aims to improve human resources through focused leadership and strategic planning, viewing education as a factor of particular importance to national development.

stories.title: CBSE introduces MITRA mentoring initiative for teachers
stories.summary: The Central Board of Secondary Education has directed its 33,287 affiliated schools to appoint three to five experienced teachers as mentors. The MITRA initiative aims to provide personalised support to in-service teachers to help them become reflective practitioners, as envisaged under the National Education Policy.

stories.title: Study highlights role of principals in teacher development
stories.summary: A South African study suggests school principals are essential for motivating teachers to engage in professional development. Researchers noted that many teachers view such training as an additional burden amidst heavy workloads and overcrowded classrooms. Principals are encouraged to create environments that enable staff to grow.

stories.title: Senate committee proposes 19% boost for Education Department
stories.summary: A Senate Appropriations Committee proposal suggests a 19 percent funding increase for the Education Department. The plan includes additional resources for special education while keeping Title I funding at current levels. The committee has identified its priorities for the upcoming fiscal year.

stories.title: Watchdog reports management issues at Education Department
stories.summary: An annual report cites interagency agreements and executive orders as primary contributors to five management challenges facing the Education Department in 2027. The agency is currently navigating these operational hurdles as it attempts to implement recent policy changes.

stories.title: East Lansing schools to host mental health film screening
stories.summary: The East Lansing Board of Education will host a screening of the film Screenagers: The Next Chapter at MacDonald Middle School on December 15. The event, organized by the district mental health coordinator, aims to examine how technology and social media influence adolescent well-being.

stories.title: Alberta asks schools to pause on new flagpoles
stories.summary: Alberta Education Minister Demetrios Nicolaides has asked school boards to pause the purchase of new outdoor flagpoles following concerns that new flag regulations could cost millions of dollars. The minister suggested that funds would be better utilized if directed toward classroom resources.

stories.title: Maine parents sue town over autistic daughter's metal rooster statues - The Washington Post
MLA proposes mandatory national anthem in P.E.I. schools
stories.summary: Progressive Conservative MLA Tyler DesRoches has introduced a proposal to make the daily playing of O Canada mandatory in all Prince Edward Island schools. DesRoches described the current inconsistency in morning traditions across the province as a missed opportunity.

stories.title: Faculty association challenges professor suspension
stories.summary: The Visva-Bharati University Faculty Association has alleged that the suspension of Professor Sudipta Bhattacharyya is intended to intimidate dissenting staff. The university vice-chancellor issued the suspension order on November 17, stating that specific charges will be provided in a future document.

stories.title: Maharashtra updates nursery admission age requirements
stories.summary: New state rules require children to be three years old by June 30 to qualify for nursery admission starting in 2027. The policy will be phased in across higher grade levels, potentially requiring some students to repeat playgroup if they do not meet the cutoff.

stories.title: Goa schools to count tiatr participation as NEP activity
stories.summary: The Goa directorate of education has instructed schools to recognize student participation in tiatr competitions as a co-curricular activity under the National Education Policy 2020. Heads of schools are directed to appoint teachers to coordinate rehearsals and encourage cultural engagement.

stories.title: Mega awareness programme on Educational Initiatives, NEP 2020 held at Poonch
stories.summary: POONCH: The School Education Department, Poonch today organised a mega awareness programme here at Government Boys Higher Secondary School to sensitise students, teachers and the general public about the eight key themes of school education and the flagship initiatives of the department. The programme commenced with a grand awareness rally,

stories.title: Kiran Bedi named national mentor for MITRA initiative
stories.summary: The National Council for Teacher Education has appointed former Puducherry Lieutenant Governor Kiran Bedi as a national mentor under the MITRA initiative. The program, established under the National Education Policy 2020, includes plans for Bedi to begin mentoring sessions for school teachers next month.

stories.summary: Oakridge Visakhapatnam Secures a Place Among India's Top 10 International Day-cum-Boarding Schools NewsVoir Visakhapatnam (Andhra Pradesh) [India], November 19: Oakridge International School, Visakhapatnam, has secured the No. 9 position nationally in the International Day-cum-Boarding category of the EducationWorld India School Rankings 2026-27. The school has also been ranked No. 1

stories.title: Oakridge Visakhapatnam ranked among top international schools
stories.summary: Oakridge International School in Visakhapatnam has been ranked ninth nationally in the international day-cum-boarding category by the EducationWorld India School Rankings 2026-27. The rankings assessed 4,500 schools across India to establish a national benchmark for educational excellence.

stories.title: Breaking Subject Barriers: How NEP 2020 is giving students more academic choices
stories.summary: NEP 2020 empowers students to combine subjects, build diverse skills and explore new career opportunities. For decades, higher education in India followed a structured pathway. Students who chose Commerce, Science or Arts largely remained within their respective disciplines throughout their academic journey. While this approach created subject expertise, it often

stories.title: Assam Medical College withdraws marriage advisory for trainees
stories.summary: Assam Medical College and Hospital withdrew an advisory asking postgraduate trainees to defer marriage until their tenure ended. The notice triggered criticism regarding the institution's authority over the personal lives of resident doctors. The advisory was withdrawn following the backlash. Personal milestones have been returned to the students.

stories.title: India considers transition to four-year law degree programmes
stories.summary: The Bar Council of India established the five-year integrated law course in 1982 to attract students directly after school. The model integrated social sciences with legal studies to standardise education. Discussions are now underway regarding a potential shift to a four-year programme. Tradition is currently under review.

stories.title: UGC identifies 32 fake universities across India
stories.summary: The University Grants Commission released a list of 32 institutions it classifies as fake, with Delhi hosting 12 of them. The Commission has urged the public to verify the recognition status of universities before enrollment. The list was shared on the official X handle of the UGC.

stories.title: NEP 2020 laying foundation for inclusive, skill-centric and future-ready education: Sukanta Majumdar - DD News
CBSE starts academic support programme in Ladakh
stories.summary: The CBSE and the Ladakh government are conducting a month-long academic support programme for class 10 and 12 students in government schools. The initiative aims to strengthen preparedness for board examinations through classroom-based support in high-altitude areas. Classes are being held across several regions in the Union Territory.
